summary: Gone D-6 cupola lookout in the Deadman Wash area north of the San Francisco Peaks; a 2020 visit found no tower foundation, only a concrete structure and benchmarks.

facts.design: D-6 cupola-style lookout, the only example of that style in Arizona per the Coconino NF photo caption
facts.status_note: A 2020 visit found the tower's own foundation no longer evident; a concrete structure on the top remains
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Coconino National Forest

access.note: Reached by Forest Road 514 on national forest land; a 2020 post drove up it and advises a four-wheel-drive vehicle

visit.trail_note: Forest Road 514 is narrow with loose cinders; four-wheel drive recommended (2020 post)

events.note: Shown on the 1962 Flagstaff topographic map
Not shown on the 1966 O'Leary Peak topographic map, which shows a different tower; the 2020 post's writer thinks the O'Leary Peak tower replaced it

evidence.supports: site is in the Deadman Wash area north of the San Francisco Peaks, accessed by Forest Road 514
evidence.quote: I was recently checking out the Deadman Wash area north of the San Francisco Peaks that is accessed Forest Road 514.

evidence.supports: writer visited and saw the remains of the Deadman fire lookout tower
evidence.quote: I drove up to check out the remains of the Deadman fire lookout tower.

evidence.supports: road is narrow with loose cinders; four-wheel drive advised
evidence.quote: The road up is a bit narrow and, because of the loose cinders, is probably best negotiated with a four-wheel drive vehicle.

evidence.supports: lookout shown on 1962 Flagstaff topo map but not on 1966 O'Leary Peak topo map
evidence.quote: The lookout is shown on the 1962 Flagstaff 1:125,000 topo map but is not shown on the 1966 O'Leary Peak 1:24,000 topo.

evidence.supports: the 1966 O'Leary Peak map shows the O'Leary Peak lookout tower instead
evidence.quote: The O'Leary Peak lookout tower is shown on the 1966 topo but not the 1962.

evidence.supports: writer's view that the O'Leary Peak tower replaced the Deadman tower
evidence.quote: The O'Leary Peak tower clearly replaced the Deadman tower and likely others

evidence.supports: writer thinks the concrete structure on top is a cistern on which a building was constructed
evidence.quote: It appears that the concrete structure is a cistern on which the building was constructed.

evidence.supports: the tower's own foundation is no longer evident
evidence.quote: The foundation for the tower itself is no longer evident.

evidence.supports: two benchmarks on the top of the hill
evidence.quote: There were two benchmarks on the top of the hill.

evidence.supports: a stone chimney on private land near the road, not at the lookout site
evidence.quote: a stone chimney not far off the road

evidence.supports: the chimney is on private land
evidence.quote: I knew from the maps I had with me that was located on private land

evidence.supports: D-6 cupola lookout style; only example in Arizona
evidence.quote: The only example of the D-6 Cupola Lookout style in Arizona.

evidence.supports: photo credit to the U.S. Forest Service, Coconino National Forest
evidence.quote: Credit U.S. Forest Service Coconino National Forest.

evidence.supports: Peakbagging lists Deadman as a lookout site (LO site) on the O'Leary Peak map
the table's LO site label means the building has been removed, or its status is unknown
evidence.quote: where the building has been removed and there may be no evidence remaining, or it's status may be unknown

evidence.supports: Deadman listed in Coconino County at 35.43628, -111.62086; type Ground; status Gone

notes_for_editor: No build year or builder appears in the sources I read. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Facebook post came up in search (snippet only, not opened) and calls it a D6 cupola built in 1928; I did not use that date because I could not read the post. The Flickr photo (uploaded 2022, photo by Phil Downum) lists several license options on its page and I could not confirm which applies, so I did not add it to photos. Access 'public' is my reading of a national forest road that a 2020 visit drove; no source states the site's legal status. The 'replaced' event is the blog writer's inference. The Forest Lookouts page for Deadman (westlookouts.weebly.com/deadman1.html) gives only the county and forest. Peakbagging's Deadman row names the O'Leary Peak map with a year of 1983, while the blog cites the 1966 O'Leary Peak topo; the story gives no Peakbagging year, so the difference is recorded here only. The story's 'no closure or private land at the site' line rests on the blog's silence; the only private land the blog mentions is a chimney off the road.
